summary: Tokan Tada (1890–1967) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Akita High School and Sera Monastery (1913–1923), he held posts at the University of Tokyo (1924), Tohoku University (1925), and the Toyo Bunko (1956).
Toke Lindegaard Knudsen specializes in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied under Kim Plofker and completed doctoral studies under David Pingree in 2008.

Tokio Takata (born 1949) specializes in Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University and the EHESS, later holding posts at Otaru University of Commerce, Kyoto University, the Toyo Bunko, and Fudan University.

Tokugen Sakai (1912–1996) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University, and under Kodo Sawaki. He held appointments at Komazawa University (1949–1987) and Eihei-ji (1977–1987).

Tokuno Oda (1860–1911) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara and Junjirō Takakusu. He taught at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Fukui Chugakko, and Toyo University.

Tokuryu Yamauchi (1890–1982) worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University, Freiburg, and under Nishida, Husserl, and Heidegger. He held professorships at Hitotsubashi University, Kyoto University, Ryukoku University, and was president of Kyoto University of Education.
Tom De Rauw works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Ann Heirman and held an academic assistant post at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Tom Ginsburg (born 1968) works in law, political science, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1985–1999) and held faculty appointments at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~2000–2008) and the University of Chicago (~2008).

Tom Hannes works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Antwerp (1988–1991) and KU Leuven (1991–1993), later holding a postdoctoral research position at Eindhoven University of Technology in 2020.

Tom Tillemans (born 1950) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Jacques May (~1980–1984) and held posts at the University of Lausanne (attested 1987–2018) and the University of Calgary (~2007).

Tomohiro Manabe specializes in Indology and philosophy. He has held academic posts as a lecturer at Waseda University (attested 2020) and as an associate professor at Hokkaido University (attested 2026).

Tomoko Masuzawa works in religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at International Christian University, Yale University, and UC Santa Barbara (PhD 1985). She held faculty posts at UNC Chapel Hill (~1987–2000) and the University of Michigan (1999).

Tomomichi Nitta works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held academic posts at Otani University as a full-time lecturer (attested 2012) and at the Otani Academic Society as a professor (attested 2026).
Tomoyasu Oshima is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied under Toshifumi Goto and held a post as a part-time lecturer at Kyoto University (attested 2012).
Tomoyuki Komine (born 1971) is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He was educated at Taisho University, where he also served as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

Tomoyuki Uno specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was affiliated with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science as a special researcher (attested 1998) and served as an assistant professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2000–2006).

Tomy Augustine works in philosophy and Indology. He studied at the University of Madras, Banaras Hindu University, and under C. S. Sundaram and Munni K. Agrawal, later holding a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

Toni Huber specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison and William Sax, and held posts at Canterbury, Victoria University of Wellington, and Humboldt University of Berlin.

Toni Schmid (1897–1972) was a Tibetology and history scholar. She studied at the University of Vienna, Lund University under Helmer Smith, and Uppsala University, and served as an antiquarian at the Royal Swedish Academy (1944–1968).

Tony K. Stewart (born 1954) specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Western Kentucky University (~1972–1976) and served on the faculties of North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and Vanderbilt University (~2011).
